analysis:
Integration of the add-on hold feature. Supplied evidence: DaemonState.addonHold (additive optional, decodeIfPresent), LifecycleMailbox/ProviderDrain owner changes, the `darkbloom addon` CLI and status line, test files, and docs/changelog. The docs describe the production invariants. Only a peer satisfying the pinned code-signing requirement (team SLDQ2GJ6TL, io.darkbloom.sandbox) may hold, with the hardened runtime and the same uid. The requested add-on id must equal the verified signer. Hold leases are 30-600 s and persist in a 0700 runtime directory with 0600 records. The hold keeps the App Attest worker and the coordinator connection, and never sends provider_drain. It reports status draining with busy fields. Only a stop preempts a hold. Update, reconnect and model-switch drains cannot reopen it. Expired leases end the hold only when ownership.lock is free.

No concrete regression is established. The trust boundary is the same-uid local user plus a signed add-on, which is already inside the TB-003 operator model. The hold is an availability lever (T-057/T-053 adjacency) but does not grant serving authorization (A-016/T-052). The state file and busy fields carry only hold metadata (add-on name, lease times, reason), with no prompts (A-001), keys or tokens.

Production sources are outside the supplied excerpts, so these remain unverified:
- AddonPeerPolicy, AddonIPCServer and ProviderLoop+AddonHold, and in particular whether any DARKBLOOM_ADDON environment override of the socket or lock path is honored in release builds.
- The cap on concurrent holds and the vm_bytes bound.
- The sanitization and length bounds of busy_addon before it reaches the coordinator.
- That hold admission, model unload and App Attest grant, revocation and connection-change handling stay authoritative at all call sites (T-053).
- The `--force` release and mailbox paths, which are bounded to the same uid.
- Whether the threat model should document the new local IPC trust boundary.

The docs state that the positive peer check is not exercised by tests, because no signed add-on is available to the runner. This is a coverage gap and not a finding.
